claude.sample_unit: physician-validated emergency vignettes (each replayed across 32 sociodemographic labels plus control)

links.outcome: Change in GPT-5 triage, testing, treatment, mental-health recommendations when sociodemographic labels varied
links.effect: GPT-5 reproduced subgroup-linked variation, with higher urgency and less advanced testing for several marginalized groups; several LGBTQIA+ labels flagged for mental-health screening in 100% of cases vs ~41–73% with GPT-4o.
links.quote: GPT-5 reproduced subgroup-linked variation, with higher assigned urgency and less advanced testing for several historically marginalized and intersectional groups.

links.outcome: Rate of adopting or elaborating on a fabricated medical detail, with and without mitigation prompt
links.effect: GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs (vs 53% for GPT-4o); a single mitigation prompt reduced this to 7.67%.
links.quote: A single mitigation prompt reduced this to 7.67%.

links.outcome: Model vulnerability to adversarial input containing one fabricated medical detail
links.effect: GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs (vs 53% for GPT-4o).
links.quote: Additionally, in an adversarial re-run that inserted one fabricated medical detail into otherwise standard clinical cases, GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs (vs 53% for GPT-4o).

links.effect: Several LGBTQIA+ labels were flagged in 100% of cases versus ~41–73% for comparable groups with GPT-4o.
links.quote: Notably, several LGBTQIA+ labels were flagged for mental-health screening in 100% of cases, versus ~41–73% for comparable groups with GPT-4o.

links.effect: GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs, versus 53% for GPT-4o.
links.quote: Additionally, in an adversarial re-run that inserted one fabricated medical detail into otherwise standard clinical cases, GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs (vs 53% for GPT-4o).

links.effect: GPT-5 showed no improvement in sociodemographic-linked decision variation and seemed worse on several endpoints compared with GPT-4o.
links.quote: Extending our validated benchmarking work, GPT-5 showed no improvement in sociodemographic-linked decision variation compared with GPT-4o and seemed to be worse on several endpoints.

unlisted_practices: A single mitigation prompt to reduce adoption or elaboration of fabricated medical details
